content.rationale:
The dependent is the flat module `src/draft_registry.rs` (szmuyqrq) that keeps draft records; it and this gate are both code artifacts, so the check is a test (code-to-code): a self-contained crate, `tests/draft_registry/` (knqkxzns), includes the module through `#[path = "../../../src/draft_registry.rs"]` and drives it over a fresh temporary directory, so the storage, naming, discovery, removal and refusal clauses are observed as files on disk rather than restated. The crate depends only on serde_json and jsonschema, the JSON and validator choices the prerequisites fix (orrvsxqq, zmmyomyp).

The check fixes the public API the module must expose so those observables are reachable. `pub fn path_for(root: &std::path::Path, handle: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf` returns exactly `<root>/<handle>.json` for any non-empty handle string, dots included — the handle is the whole stem, so `a.b` names `<root>/a.b.json` and never `<root>/a.json`; `pub fn write(root: &std::path::Path, document: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), Error>` creates the registry root when it is not there and stores one document at the path its `handle` names, replacing rather than appending; `pub fn read(root: &std::path::Path, handle: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, Error>` returns that document or a named refusal, and a path that cannot be read for any reason other than absence — whatever the failure's kind: a directory where the document would be, a symlink loop, a permission failure — is `Error::Io` naming that path, never `Error::Missing`, and a document that is not JSON, including bytes that are not UTF-8, is `Error::NotJson`, never `Error::Io`; `pub fn scan(root: &std::path::Path) -> Result<Vec<(String, serde_json::Value)>, Error>` returns every `.json` document keyed by the handle its filename gives, and reaches each document through the same `read` that serves a single record, so a document `read` refuses fails the whole scan with that refusal instead of being dropped from the list; `pub fn remove(root: &std::path::Path, handle: &str) -> Result<(), Error>` removes exactly the one document at the path the handle names, `<root>/<handle>.json`, and leaves every other document untouched; it removes that document without reading or validating it, so a non-conforming target is discarded like a conforming one; a handle the directory does not name is the same absence `read` answers, `Error::Missing` carrying that path, while any other filesystem failure is `Error::Io` naming the path, not a panic and not a silent success; it calls `remove_file` on that path and classifies the error rather than pre-checking existence, so a path that cannot be examined is `Io`, not absence. `Error` is a public enum with the variants `Missing(std::path::PathBuf)`, `NotJson(std::path::PathBuf, serde_json::Error)`, `Invalid(std::path::PathBuf, String)`, `HandleMismatch { path: std::path::PathBuf, filename: String, handle: String }` and `Io(std::io::Error)`; it derives `Debug`, implements `Display`, and every refusal names the path it refused. `root` is the registry directory the caller supplies (`.deccy/work/`), so the tests never depend on the current directory or on a real repository. The API is the gate's observable contract, not a restatement of the decision's wording: any implementation that stores, names, scans, removes and refuses as these clauses require satisfies it, and a rewording of the decision does not change it.

The use of each prerequisite is checked through those observables. rqtowtqn and twpvqstu fix that a record is exactly one JSON document at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, its filename the record's handle, and that records are found only by scanning that directory: the gate asserts the exact path from `path_for` for a plain handle and for a handle carrying a dot, so `a.b` is `<root>/a.b.json` and not `<root>/a.json`, that a write lands at `<handle>.json` and nowhere else, that two handles leave two documents, that a re-write replaces instead of appending, that a landed record reads like an open one, and that `scan` returns every `.json` document — including one placed on disk by hand, so discovery reads the directory rather than an index. twpvqstu also fixes that discarding an open draft removes the one document at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, leaves every other record at its handle, and never takes a landed record away: the gate removes a written open record and a document placed on disk by hand, asserts that only the named document vanishes and that a landed sibling, a hand-placed sibling and a document `read` refuses stay exactly where they were, and asserts that removing an absent handle is a named `Missing` refusal that does not touch the records that are there. The removal is also checked as the path operation the decision fixes, with four further observables. First, the target is removed without being interpreted: the gate places a non-conforming document at the path the handle names — once malformed bytes and once JSON that fails `schemas/work.json` — and asserts that `remove` still returns `Ok(())` and the document is gone, while a conforming sibling stays byte-identical, so a removal that reads, parses or validates the target before deleting it fails the check. Second, removal never deletes the registry root: the gate removes the one document from a root the first write created and asserts that the root is still there and is a directory, that `scan` of it returns an empty list, and that a later write and removal under the same root still work, so an implementation that deletes the emptied root — or that otherwise changes anything but the document at the handle's path — fails. Third, only `NotFound` is `Missing` and every other filesystem failure is `Io`, whatever its kind, not just is-a-directory: the gate induces four different non-`NotFound` failures at the target path — a directory where the document would be, a read-only registry root that makes the removal fail with permission-denied, an unsearchable registry root (mode `0o000`) that makes the path itself unexaminable, and a registry root that is a regular file so that unlinking the document fails with not-a-directory, a kind other than permission-denied — and asserts that each refusal is `Error::Io` and not `Error::Missing`, that it names the path, and that nothing else in the directory is removed; for the regular-file root it also asserts that the root file is left byte-identical. The unsearchable root is the pre-check the removal must not make: `Path::exists`, `Path::is_file` and `Path::metadata` swallow the stat failure and answer `false`, so a removal written as `if !path.exists() { Missing }` (or with either other pre-check) reports a document that is still there as absent instead of calling `remove_file` and classifying its error; the gate asserts that the document survives the failed removal, that it reads once the root is searchable again, and that the removal then succeeds. A process that can unlink through an unsearchable root (running as root) skips the case, never weakened to accept `Missing`; the same mapping is checked for `read`, where a directory at the record's path and a symlink loop at the record's path are each `Io` naming that path and never `Missing`, so a read that maps every io error to absence, or that special-cases only is-a-directory, fails. Fourth, a dotted handle removes exactly its own document: the gate places `<root>/a.b.json` and `<root>/a.json`, removes `a.b`, and asserts that the first is gone and that the second, the document of the handle `a`, is untouched. nolspvpw fixes the registry as a directory of untracked state and names it as where durable draft state is written, `.deccy/work/`: the gate hands `write` a root that is not there and asserts the write creates it, stores the record under it and leaves `read` and `scan` finding that record, so the registry the write is given is made by the write that stores the first record rather than by an earlier step. The gate touches only its temporary directory: no change, no node, no graph. owyntkvw fixes the handle as the record's identity and the other fields as references: the gate keys every document and every scan entry by the handle, never by the node or the edit. wrvsxwmq fixes the document's closed form in `schemas/work.json`, and the module embeds that schema with `include_str!("../schemas/work.json")` and compiles it in-process with the `jsonschema` crate (zmmyomyp): the gate asserts that a document missing a required field, a document with an unknown field, malformed JSON, and a document whose bytes are not UTF-8 are each refused — the last two as `NotJson` wherever they are not JSON — with the path named in the refusal, so a document that is not JSON is never reported as `Io`, and that a conforming open and a conforming landed record both read. ntypuupx fixes that reading a record refuses a document that does not conform to `schemas/work.json` or whose `handle` is not the handle its filename gives: the gate asserts that such a document is refused with `HandleMismatch` and that the refusal is an `Err` value — not a panic and not a silent skip. Discovery is held to the same refusal: with one conforming record and one refused document in the directory, `scan` returns an `Err` naming the offending path — checked for a document missing a required field and for a document whose handle is not its filename — never `Ok` with the bad document dropped and never `Ok` with it included unchecked. szmuyqrq fixes the module as the single flat file `src/draft_registry.rs`, which is the path the shim includes, and knqkxzns fixes the test as a self-contained crate with its own fixtures.

Scan over an absent directory is fixed as `Ok(Vec::new())`: only a directory that is not there yields an empty list, because the registry is the list of documents that are there and a directory that does not exist holds no records. An existing root that cannot be listed — a path that is not a directory, or a directory the process cannot search — is `Io` naming the path, never a false empty registry; the gate drives `scan` over a regular file at the root path and over a root made unsearchable with mode `0o000` and asserts `Io` in both, never `Ok(Vec::new())`, so a scan that returns an empty list for every `read_dir` error fails. The root the registry names is the first write's to create: the gate hands `write` a root that is not there and asserts the root and `<handle>.json` under it, with the stored document read and scanned back and its bytes identical to the same document written under a root that already existed, so creating the root neither adds to nor takes from the record. A second write into the root the first one made replaces the document there rather than appending a second one. A document that fails the schema is still refused with `Invalid` naming the path it would have been stored at, leaving no record document and an empty scan; the gate does not demand whether a refused write creates the root, because the first-write clause covers the write that stores a record, not what a refusal leaves behind. Nothing here fixes how a refusal is printed, which exit status a verb uses, or how the schema is located at run time. The gate requires `remove` to delete the named document without reading or validating it — a non-conforming target is discarded like a conforming one — and does not require it to refuse a landed handle: the landed end is kept because a discard names a draft that did not land, so the gate checks the landed record as a sibling that survives the removal rather than as a state the operation must inspect. Nothing here fixes which io error kind a platform reports for a failing path, only that a failure that is not `NotFound` is reported as `Io` whatever its kind, and that a document that is not JSON — including bytes that are not UTF-8 — is reported as `NotJson` and never as `Io`. A case the platform cannot provoke (a process that writes or unlinks through a read-only or unsearchable directory, a platform without symlinks) is skipped or gated by platform, never weakened to accept `Missing`.
